question.problem:
The force $F,$ measured in newtons $(\text{N})$, needed to extend a spring by some length $l,$ measured in $\text{m},$ is directly proportional to $l.$ When the extension of the spring is $l=0.005\,\text{m},$ the force on the spring is $F=25\,\text{N}.$ What is the constant of variation?

The constant of variation is
{{field-1}}$\text{N/m}.$
question.worked_solution:
The force $F$ is directly proportional to the extension $l,$ so we have

$$
F=kl,
$$

where $k$ is the constant of variation.

We are told that when the extension is $l=0.005\,\text{m},$ the force is $F=25\,\text{N}.$ We can use this information to solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}25 & =k\cdot (0.005) \\ 25 & =0.005k \\ \frac{25}{0.005} & =k \\ 5\,000 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $k=\frac{F}{l},$ we have that the units of $k$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{N}}{\text{m}} & =\text{N/m}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our final answer is $k=5\,000\,\text{N/m}.$
